target_customer: Families and groups booking connecting rooms and luxury hotel suites
problem: Hotel booking sites sell standard king and queen rooms and list few suites or connecting rooms, so groups had to phone or email hotels.
business_model: commission on hotel suite bookings with member rates
product_category: online travel booking for suites and connecting rooms

founders.name: Kyle Killion
founders.background_notes: Source: https://hackernoon.com/founder-interviews-kyle-killion-of-suiteness-6c8887327d88; YC page lists Apartment List, Yelp and Coupa.

founders.name: Robbie Bhathal
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch July 2016 and the YC page; December 2016 press release names him CEO.

competitors.name: Airbnb
competitors.what: home rentals as the alternative for families wanting multiple bedrooms

competitors.name: HomeAway and VRBO
competitors.what: vacation rentals the company positioned itself against as an upscale alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking front end plus hotel inventory integrations; the hard part was hotel contracting, not code.

defensibility.rationale: Direct contracts for connecting rooms are a modest supply moat, but large online travel agencies could add suite listings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The founder's account says Expedia and Booking list only a few suites; no sourced evidence they copied the connecting room wedge. Suiteness remained live with about 4,100 hotels per its site.

market_need_then: TechCrunch July 2016: most hotel booking platforms only handle king or queen room types so suites were poorly listed; the company said many hotels do not allow online booking of high-end suites.

branding.name_origin: Not explained directly; the founder interview says the company was renamed Suiteness when Flights With Friends shut down and the focus moved to suites.

identity.voice_and_tone: warm and aspirational, 'You deserve more. You deserve better.', described as socially conscious positive luxury

branding.brand_signature: the suite-only positioning and charity donation per booking

rebrands.why: pivot to suite booking; keeping With Friends drew a legal threat from Zynga per the founder interview

brand_strength.rationale: Name states the niche and the voice is consistent, but no evidence of community or press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Flights With Friends, a real-time trip planning app
pivots.to: Suiteness, a booking platform for suites and connecting rooms
pivots.why: the travel hero planners wanted multi-bedroom suites, per the founder interview

outcome_analysis: Suiteness pivoted from a trip planning app to a suite and connecting room booking site, raised $1M in December 2015 and a $5M Series A in December 2016, and still operates with member rates at about 4,100 hotels. No acquisition or shutdown was found. It stayed a niche travel marketplace and did not report later large rounds in sources found.
notes: Stephen Caudill is described in the Hackernoon interview as software architect and one of 'the three of us' but not explicitly called co-founder, so not listed. CB Insights total ($10.62M and $11.12M in different pages) exceeds the two recorded rounds; gap unexplained, may include PPP loan. The December 2015 round label was not stated so recorded as other; its source is from the search result title. YC page lists founding year 2012 while another source says 2014. Competitors as of 2016-07 to 2016-12; the Dec 2016 release is three months after the batch.
